FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (Part 3) (Second revision) was adopted by Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized 
by the Interconnection and Information Exchange Among IT Eguipment and Systems Sectional Committee had been 
approved by the Electronics and Information Technology Division Council. 


In India, the communications broadcasted by Government (state or central) and other entities in many occasions 
(like emergency situations or bulk SMS to subscribers/customers from banks and treasuries etc) for all or select 
citizens, are mostly sent in English or in Hindi. However, most of the citizen are more comfortable and would prefer 
such communications in their local/regional language. The lack of text inputting/display facility in local/regional 
languages in mobile phones was creating the communication barrier. This Indian Standard was, therefore, developed 
keeping the idea that the citizen should be able to send and receive messages (communications) at least in one of the 
officially recognized Indian language of their choice. 


The standard is set to leverage the strength of mobile penetration in the country for transmitting the text message to the 
citizens in their regional language, particularly in hours of disaster management. 


This standard was originally published in 2016 based on the reguest from Ministry of Electronics and Information 
Technology (MeitY) (erstwhile DeitY). 


The first revision incorporated Amendment 1 to IS 16333 (Part 3) : 2016 and was done to take care of the limitations 
of various types of mobile phones in implementing character sets of various Indian languages. The second revision 
has been undertaken to ease the process of verifying compliance to text-input and display function capability of Indian 
languages, based on the experience of manufactures and testing laboratories during the implementation of the standard. 


The major modifications incorporated in this revision are: 


a) Provision of choosing keyboard layout of manufacturers choice for inputting various Indian Languages 
has been added as Note 4 under clause 5; and 


b) Modifications in optional and mandatory characters in the Annex B (optional reguirements) are given 
below. 


The following characters have been added in Annex B (optional reguirements) . 


Character Language

it was observed that these characters are used frequently: 


a) 20B9 from every language in Annex B; 
b) 02BC in Assamese Language (Table B.1); and 
c) 0965 in Bangla language (Table B.2).

IS 16333 (Part 3) : 2022 


Indian Standard 


MOBILE PHONE HANDSETS 


PART 3 INDIAN LANGUAGE SUPPORT FOR MOBILE PHONE HANDSETS — 
SPECIFIC REOUIREMENTS 


(Second Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard (Part 3) defines the reguirements for 
mobile phone handsets for inputting of text in English, 
Hindi and at least one additional Indian official 
language along with facility of message readability for 
all 22 Indian official languages. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standard given below contains provisions, which 
through reference in this text constitute provisions of 
this standard. At the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are subject to 
revision, and parties to agreement based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of the standards 
listed as follows: 


IS No. Title 
16333 Mobile phone handsets: 
(Part 1) : 2015 Part 1 Safety reguirements 
16350 : 2016 Enhanced in script key board 


layout. 


3 TERMS AND DEFINITIONS 


For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given in 
IS 16333 (Part 1) and the following shall apply. 


3.1 Indian Official Languages — The Constitution 
of India designates a bilingual approach for official 
language of the Government of India employing 
usage of Hindi written in the Devanagari script, as 
well as English. Hindi and English find everyday use 
for important official purposes, such as parliamentary 
proceedings, judiciary, communications between the 
Central Government and the State Government. States 
within India have the liberty and powers to specify 
their own official language(s) through legislation and 
presently there are 22 Indian official languages namely, 
Assamese, Bengali, Bodo, Dogri, Gujarati, Hindi, 
Kannada, Kashmiri, Konkani, Maithili, Malayalam, 
Manipuri, Marathi, Nepali, Oriya, Punjabi, Sanskrit, 
Sindhi, Santhali, Tamil, Telugu and Urdu as given in 
the eighth schedule of Indian constitution. 


3.2 Third Indian Language — Any of the officially 
recognized Indian language except English and Hindi. 


4 REOUIREMENTS 


The mobile phone handsets shall have inbuilt capability 
to support the Indian official languages for this purpose. 


4.1 The mobile phone handsets shall have facility for 
inputting of text in English, Hindi and at least one 
additional Indian official language. The third language 
that is to be supported by mobile phone handsets shall 
be decided by phone manufacturer/supplier. 


4.2 Message readability in the mobile phone handsets 
shall be provided for all 22 Indian official languages 
and English. 


5 TESTS 


5.1 The reguirement of inputting of text given under 4.1 
shall be verified by inputting of all the characters: 


a) In English, as per Annex A in the mobile phone 
handsets. 


b) In Hindi and in the additional (third) Indian official 
language declared by the manufacturer, as given 
in IS 16350 in the mobile phone handsets. Out of 
all the characters specified in IS 16350, characters 
corresponding to the code points mentioned in 
Annex B are optional. 


5.2 The reguirement of message readability as given 
under 4.2 shall be verified by sending the text from 
some other device, by inputting all the characters: 


a) In English, as per Annex A and display of the same 
on the mobile phone handsets at the receiving end. 


b) In all the 22 Indian official languages, as given in 
IS 16350 and display of the same on the mobile 
phone handsets at the receiving end. 

NOTES 

1 The shapes of the reference glyphs used in the code 
point charts given in IS 16350 are not prescriptive 
(are only representative). Considerable variation (in shape and 
proportion) is to be expected in actual fonts as manufacturers 
and font designers may use different fonts. 

2 If the presentation of characters displayed on mobile phones 
are different from that of the characters displayed in IS 16350 
due to font variation, then the manufacturer shall provide a 
comparison chart for the variations at the time of testing. 

3 Characters mentioned in Annex C shall be Represented 
(in storage) by normalized form mentioned in Annex C. 


IS 16333 (Part 3) : 2022 


4 The facility for inputting of text in English, Hindi and one 
additional Indian official language are not restricted to any 
particular keyboard layout or input mechanism. When the 
corresponding glyph of a code-point defined in this standard 
is not on the physical/virtual keyboard layout, then the 
manufacturer/solution provider shall provide instructions on 


how to input that code-point. 


6 MARKING 


Each mobile phone handsets shall be packed with an 
instruction manual to furnish the following information 
in addition to the information given in 5.1 of IS 16333 
(Part 1). 


6.1 The Indian official languages that the mobile phone 
handset is capable of sending the text in. 


6.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the reguirements of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules 
and Regulations framed thereunder, and the products 
may be marked with the Standard Mark. 


IS 16333 (Part 3) : 2022

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and guality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enguiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Head (Publication & Sales), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically, a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed, if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in.
